positions.description:

- Developed and maintained a robotics data web-based visualization tool using React, which
supported different ways of viewing data (3D, plotting and log filtering, for example), and streaming
the data from different sources.
- Developed a framework and pipeline used to transform, process and combine different debugging artifacts into a single visualization file. Used Python, Docker and AWS CDK.

Node.js and AWS CDK for the backend and infrastructure, React for the web frontend.
- Developed a service to sync status from different internal services and Jira. Used Java, and AWS
CDK for infrastructure.

projects.title: Development of an instrument to measure and analyze critical thinking through argumentation in third and fourth grade students
projects.description:
Critical thinking is an essential ability in problem solving, which consists in analyzing, understanding and evaluating a given situation. By measuring this (specifically in children), we can get a general vision of the cognitive process and the analysis done, considering the final answer to a given question.

However, the problem we face when trying to measure this skill is the tradeoff between giving the student the tools he or she needs to explain the mental process, trying to maintain the greatest freedom of expression when answering, while restricted to an evaluation system that allows us to analyze the answer, so that we may get the most out of the results.

To solve this problem, in this research we developed an evaluation tool based on comics, taking advantage of the technology to create an instrument that could be used in tablets, as well as computers.

Said tool uses an adapted version of the story “Around The World In 80 Days”, along an argumentation system, where the children can build their own answer.

Alongside this, the research focuses on analyzing the differences in the results found when comparing this application to the paper version of the tool (which uses the same story and questions), which was validated previously.

projects.title: Comic-based dynamic assessment instrument for measuring reading comprehension among third grade students
projects.description:
Reading comprehension is a multifaceted construct; assessing reading comprehension therefore requires multiple indicators in order to measure the underlying variables and avoid mono-operation bias. Dynamic assessment methods may provide a good alternative as they are capable of adapting to and measuring a student’s level. In addition to this, students are drawn to comics through intrinsic motivation, making them attractive as an assessment instrument.

The research question that guides this study therefore asks “How effective is a comic-based, dynamic assessment instrument at measuring reading comprehension?”

To answer this question, an instrument was developed for use with a tablet. This instrument was validated internally and externally using a standardized test and the students’ grades. The instrument correctly measured the students’ level of reading comprehension, regardless of what that level may have been.

The dynamic assessment instrument described in this paper allows the students’ level of reading comprehension to be measured and understood, providing the results in real time. As an internet-based test, the instrument can be easily accessed by a large number of students at the same time. Using this type of instrument in the classroom facilitates Formative Assessment, using the students’ actions and mistakes as an opportunity for learning, as well as to guide and modify the teacher’s activities in the classroom.
